[Open the BPMN source](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/blob/main/cat-harness/library/processes/document-ingestion.bpmn){: .btn .btn-outline }

They are not the same directory under two names:

| | `uploads/` | `library/<bib-slug>/` |
|---|---|---|
| what it holds | raw files as dropped | ingested, structured, described |
| stage | incoming queue | **L1 source content** |
| greppable by the corpus checklist | **no** | yes |

The corpus-grep checklist searches `library/` only, so a source still sitting
in `uploads/` makes a **clean grep** read as *"nobody has done this"*. An
un-ingested source is worse than an absent one: it produces false confidence
rather than a gap.

## `library/` is L1
{: #library-is-l1 data-fa-label="sec:document-ingestion-library-is-l1" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core/edit/main/docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/library-is-l1.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/library-is-l1.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/library-is-l1.md" data-repo="litlfred/folio-assistant-core" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="library-is-l1.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/library-is-l1.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="library-is-l1.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/library-is-l1.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Anything under `library/` is **L1 source content**. Any knowledge-graph
reference to a source — from a paper, an L2 DAK, an L3 IG, or any other
artefact — resolves to it **through `library/`**, never to a loose path or a
bare URL.

A bibliography entry may point at a **remote** asset rather than a local
binary. That lives in a sibling `assets[]` field carrying kind / role /
url-or-path / checksum / retrieved — **not** inside `library:`, because
`LibraryRef` is regenerated from the tree on every sync and an authored URL
placed there is silently dropped.

## What is in a library entry folder
{: #the-library-entry-folder data-fa-label="sec:document-ingestion-the-library-entry-folder" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core/edit/main/docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/the-library-entry-folder.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/the-library-entry-folder.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/the-library-entry-folder.md" data-repo="litlfred/folio-assistant-core" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="the-library-entry-folder.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/the-library-entry-folder.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="the-library-entry-folder.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/the-library-entry-folder.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Each ingested document is one folder, `library/<doc>/`, named by its
bibliography slug. This is every file and folder it can hold, the schema that
checks it, and what writes it. **Required** means the
[L1 completeness gate](#the-l1-completeness-gate) fails without it; the others
are written when the document has that kind of content.

| file | what it is | schema | written by | required |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `manifest.jsonld` | the entry's own node: a `SourceDocument` with its title, provenance, licence keys and the list of its sections | [`library-nodes`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/library-nodes.html' | relative_url }}) | `gen-library-jsonld` | yes |
| `structure.json` | the document's table of contents: its sections, their pages and whether the outline was read or inferred | [`document-structure`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/document-structure.html' | relative_url }}), [`pdf-structure`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/pdf-structure.html' | relative_url }}) | the structure arm (`pdf-structure`, or the slides, notebook or text arm) | yes |
| `sections/` | one `.md` (the verbatim text) and one `.jsonld` (a `doco:Section`) per section | [`library-nodes`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/library-nodes.html' | relative_url }}) | `gen-library-jsonld` | yes |
| `blocks/` | the typed statements extracted from sections, such as a recommendation or a requirement, each `derivedFrom` its section | [`library-nodes`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/library-nodes.html' | relative_url }}), [`block-kinds`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/block-kinds.html' | relative_url }}) | `gen-library-jsonld`, from `candidates.json` | yes |
| `candidates.json` | the proposals the blocks are made from, before they become blocks | [`ingest-candidates`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/ingest-candidates.html' | relative_url }}) | `extract-candidates` | when requirements or recommendations are extracted |
| `licence.json` | the source's licence, as one record | [`source-licence`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/source-licence.html' | relative_url }}) | `ingest-document` | yes |
| `summaries.json` | an agent's draft summary of each prose block, kept beside the block and never replacing its text | [`block-summary`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/block-summary.html' | relative_url }}) | `cat summaries` | advisory |
| `images.json` and `images/` | the images placed in the document, with their descriptions | [`document-image`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/document-image.html' | relative_url }}) | the image arm (`pdf-images`) | when the document has images |
| `vector-figures.json`, `vector-labels.json` and `figures/` | figures drawn as vectors, and the labels positioned on them | [`vector-figure`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/vector-figure.html' | relative_url }}), [`vector-labels`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/vector-labels.html' | relative_url }}) | the vector arm (`pdf-vector-figures`, `pdf-vector-labels`) | when the document has vector figures |
| `keywords.json` | the entry's keywords. Being retired: keywords are extracted content, so they are now built when the site is published, on the [Keywords]({{ '/en/cat-harness/lsi/keywords/' | relative_url }}) page | [`library-keywords`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/library-keywords.html' | relative_url }}) | `library-keywords` | no |
| `referenced.json` | for a source the library records but does not hold: where it is and how to get it | [`referenced-source`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/referenced-source.html' | relative_url }}) | `referenced-source` | instead of the text, for a referenced source |
| `README.md` | a generated summary of the entry for someone browsing the repository | none | `subgraph-readmes` | no |

Tables, archives and recordings add their own records
([`tabular-csvw`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/tabular-csvw.html' | relative_url }}),
[`archive-contents`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/archive-contents.html' | relative_url }}),
[`recording`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/recording.html' | relative_url }})).
A layer above may add its own files too, such as the DAK layer's L1 library
graph.

**Two records live outside the folder.** The intake record for the original
upload stays with it in `uploads/`
([`intake`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/intake.html' | relative_url }})). A
catalogue's Dublin Core record is kept in the catalogue, not in the entry
([`dublin-core`]({{ '/folio-assistant-core/schema/dublin-core.html' | relative_url }}),
[`catalogue`]({{ '/folio-assistant-core/schema/catalogue.html' | relative_url }})).

**The entry's address.** The entry is named by
`assets/library/jsonld/<instance>/source/<doc>` on the site: its manifest is
published at that address plus `.jsonld`, and a small page at the address
itself points to the entry's library page. The library page for the entry is a rendering of it, with its own
address ([`library-iri`]({{ '/cat-harness/schema/library-iri.html' | relative_url }})).

To see whether a given folder is complete, run
`bun run cat check:l1-complete library/<doc>`: it reports each requirement
above as met, unmet or not yet derivable.

<div class="bpmn-figure" id="figure-the-pipeline">
  <img src="{{ '/assets/img/workflows/l1-document-ingestion.svg' | relative_url }}"
       alt="BPMN swimlane diagram: the basic ingestion flow is called first — the upload is accepted, its metadata goes into the knowledge graph and the asset is catalogued in library; the Ingestion Engine then detects its media type and mints a doc id, then calls four subprocesses in turn — extract structure, derive content, build the L1 knowledge graph, and the L1 completeness gate; an incomplete result opens a bean on the shared work plan and returns to the derive step, while a complete one is moved into library under its bibliography slug and becomes citeable as an L1 source.">
</div>

[Open the BPMN source](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core/blob/main/collab/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn){: .btn .btn-outline }

**It begins by calling the basic flow.** The first step is a call into
`document-ingestion.bpmn`, the basic ingestion flow every asset takes: the
upload is accepted, its metadata goes into the knowledge graph, and the asset is
catalogued in `library/`. That flow makes no content-type decision; everything
after the call is the document-specific refinement.

**The Ingestion Engine is an actor, not a script.** It runs unattended. A drop
during an editing session triggers ingestion in the background — the
contributor does not wait for it, and nothing about the editing flow blocks on
it.

**The failure edge is a bean, not a log line.** When the completeness gate finds
a missing derived artefact, the engine opens a bean and the document **stays in
`uploads/`**. It does not land half-ingested in `library/` looking finished.

**Each subprocess is its own file**, called with `bpmn:callActivity` and
declared with `bpmn:import`, so each opens on its own in bpmn.io.

**The end is where authoring begins.** "Available to cite as an L1 source" is
the hand-off into [the publication workflow](../process/publication-workflow.html) — the
same corpus an author edits and a reviewer reviews.

       alt="BPMN diagram: from a binary, an exclusive gateway asks whether there is an embedded text layer; if yes the text layer is extracted, if no the document is OCR'd to per-page text files; both paths split the result into section markdown files carrying a document brief, then write structure.json and extract claim candidates.">

[Open the BPMN source](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core/blob/main/processes/library/ingest-extract-structure.bpmn){: .btn .btn-outline }

The OCR branch is the one to know about. A document ingested that way keeps its
text in `ocr/page-*.txt` and only a **stub** in `sections/` — so the documented
`sections/` grep cannot see its mathematics at all. That asymmetry is why the
corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier, and why a clean `sections/` grep is not
evidence that the library lacks a topic.

Each section file carries the document brief in its front-matter (contextual
retrieval), so a hit is interpretable without opening anything else.

The last step is the one that cannot be retrofitted. A generated description
is **a claim by someone**, not a property of the file. Recording whether a
human or an agent wrote it — and for an agent, which model version — lets a
reader weigh it and makes a superseded model's descriptions findable as a set.
It is unrecoverable once lost.

<div class="bpmn-figure" id="figure-ingest-the-theme">
  <img src="{{ '/assets/img/workflows/ingest-theme.svg' | relative_url }}"
       alt="BPMN diagram: from a theme source in hand, an exclusive gateway asks whether the theme is served by a deployment or stated by a style guide; the served stylesheet's declarations or the guide's own rules are read, values are mapped onto the shared palette roles, contradictions in the source are recorded, and a gateway asks whether every layout is present — if not the subprocess ends refused as incomplete, if so a theme and UI review produces the Theme node.">
</div>

[Open the BPMN source](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/blob/main/processes/ingest-theme.bpmn){: .btn .btn-outline }

**Only some sources are themes, and a person decides which.** After content is
derived, the gateway *A theme source?* asks whoever is ingesting whether this
document also carries a theme: a deployed site that serves one, or a style
guide that states one. No rule computes the answer: whether a branded document is a theme source is
an authoring judgement. A source that is not a theme skips straight to
building the knowledge graph.

The decision sits at a gateway, not inside the subprocess, because "this is
not a theme" (the normal case) and "this theme is malformed" (a defect, which
the subprocess reports by refusing) are different outcomes.

Inside, the two kinds of source differ in one step only: a deployment's
**served** stylesheet is read for its declarations, while a guide's **stated**
rules are read as it writes them. After that the paths join:

- values are mapped onto the shared palette **roles**;
- contradictions **in the source** are recorded as data, never silently resolved
  by picking one;
- a value the source is silent on is marked as a choice, not presented as a
  measurement;
- if a layout is missing, the subprocess **refuses** as incomplete rather than
  producing a theme quietly degraded to the layouts it was given.

A complete theme goes to the theme and UI review, and the result is one Theme
node: one kind, because the palette vocabulary is shared and only the geometry
varies between a sticky, a webpage and a publication.

Each folder gets a **standalone `dublin-core.jsonld`** as its record of truth,
referenced from `manifest.jsonld`. `dcterms` is already this corpus's JSON-LD
vocabulary, so this extends a live context rather than introducing one.

The folder name **is** the bibliography citation key, so a citation and a
directory are the same string.

[Open the BPMN source](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core/blob/main/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn){: .btn .btn-outline }

The gate makes every derivation step above obligatory: an incomplete document
is refused promotion and stays out of `library/`.

The translation check is a **round trip**. A forward-only check asks whether
the target-language text reads well, which a confident mistranslation passes.
Back-translating and comparing asks whether the *meaning* survived, and needs
no reference translation. It cannot decide which reading is right; that goes to
a reviewer.

## Running it
{: #what-is-not-built-yet data-fa-label="sec:document-ingestion-what-is-not-built-yet" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core/edit/main/docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/what-is-not-built-yet.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/what-is-not-built-yet.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/what-is-not-built-yet.md" data-repo="litlfred/folio-assistant-core" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="what-is-not-built-yet.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/what-is-not-built-yet.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="what-is-not-built-yet.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/what-is-not-built-yet.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

The path is two commands, and `check:l1-complete` is the gate between them:

```sh
bun run cat ingest uploads/FILE.pdf --library <lib>            # rung + every derived arm, into ingest-staging/
bun run cat ingest uploads/FILE.pdf --library <lib> --promote  # the L1 gate, then into <lib>/<slug>/
```

The gate reports each requirement as **met**, **unmet** or **not yet
derivable**: a per-format arm (images, audio, tables, archives) that cannot run
does not read as a pass. The method, rung by rung, is the
[`l1-document-ingestion`]({{ '/reference/skill-instructions/l1-document-ingestion.html' | relative_url }})
skill; audio and tables have their own,
[`audio-transcription`]({{ '/reference/skill-instructions/audio-transcription.html' | relative_url }})
and
[`tabular-metadata`]({{ '/reference/skill-instructions/tabular-metadata.html' | relative_url }}).

## How much of this does Dublin Core carry?
{: #how-much-of-this-does-dublin-core-carry data-fa-label="sec:document-ingestion-how-much-of-this-does-dublin-core-carry" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core/edit/main/docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/how-much-of-this-does-dublin-core-carry.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/how-much-of-this-does-dublin-core-carry.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/how-much-of-this-does-dublin-core-carry.md" data-repo="litlfred/folio-assistant-core" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="how-much-of-this-does-dublin-core-carry.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/how-much-of-this-does-dublin-core-carry.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="how-much-of-this-does-dublin-core-carry.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/how-much-of-this-does-dublin-core-carry.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Some of it. The answer decides whether a field is a `dcterms` term or one in
this project's own namespace.

**Dublin Core covers the bibliographic layer well** — `dcterms:title`,
`creator`, `date`, `language`, `identifier`, `hasPart`, `format`, `extent`. The
per-folder record and the archive's part/whole structure sit comfortably there.

**It does not cover the derived layer.** A narrative description of a figure, a
transcript, a back-translation confidence, a sheet's column headers, and above
all the **provenance of a generated narrative** are not `dcterms` terms, and a
published vocabulary is the wrong place to guess an IRI.

The house rule already in `schemas/jsonld.ts` decides the shape: *generalising
is sound; inventing is not.* Where an existing vocabulary has the term, use it;
where it does not, the term goes in this project's own namespace rather than
being bent into an approximate `dcterms` one. Which vocabularies to reach for
first — PROV-O for provenance is the obvious candidate — is **not yet decided**
and must be settled against the published specifications rather than from
memory.

## Editing an ingested source
{: #editing-an-ingested-source data-fa-label="sec:document-ingestion-editing-an-ingested-source" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core/edit/main/docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/editing-an-ingested-source.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/editing-an-ingested-source.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-document-ingestion/editing-an-ingested-source.md" data-repo="litlfred/folio-assistant-core" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="editing-an-ingested-source.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/editing-an-ingested-source.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="editing-an-ingested-source.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/editing-an-ingested-source.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/guides-document-ingestion/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Ingestion never edits corpus content. It produces L1 records; authoring and
review consume them through the ordinary flow in
[the publication workflow](../process/publication-workflow.html), where a change to a
content block goes through validation, findings, and an editor's decision.

One coupling: a drop into `uploads/` **during** an editing
session starts ingestion in the background. The editor is not blocked, and the
new source becomes citeable when the gate passes — not before.
